title: White vs. brown eggs: are there nutrition differences?

seo.title: White vs. brown eggs: nutrition differences explained
seo.meta_description: Brown eggs are not inherently more nutritious than white eggs. USDA says shell color is determined by hen breed and does not significantly change nutrient levels.
seo.search_intent: Find out whether brown eggs are more nutritious than white eggs

excerpt: USDA states that shell color does not significantly affect egg nutrients: breed determines whether a hen lays white, brown or other-colored eggs. Diet, egg size and deliberate nutrient enrichment can alter composition, but those factors are separate from shell color.
content_html:
Brown eggs often cost more and can look more “farm-like,” but shell color is not a nutrition grade.

What USDA says

USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service states that the breed of the hen determines shell color and that nutrient levels are not significantly different between white- and brown-shell eggs.

Why can brown eggs cost more?

Breed economics are one reason. USDA notes that brown-egg-laying hens have historically tended to be larger or less feed-efficient, which can increase production costs. Retail price also reflects housing claims, brand, organic certification and local demand.

What actually can change egg nutrition?

Hen diet can alter certain nutrients. Omega-3-enriched eggs, for example, come from feeding strategies designed to change fatty-acid content. Either a white or brown egg can be nutritionally enriched.

Egg size matters too. A 60 g egg naturally contains more calories and protein than a 50 g egg simply because there is more egg.

Does a darker yolk mean a better egg?

Yolk color responds strongly to pigments in the hen's diet. A deeper orange yolk does not automatically mean more protein, better safety or greater freshness.

Choose shell color for preference if you like; use the label and production claims for information that actually changes what you are buying.

faq.question: Are brown eggs more nutritious?
faq.answer: No. USDA says nutrient levels are not significantly different because of shell color.

faq.question: What determines shell color?
faq.answer: Primarily the hen's breed and genetics.

faq.question: Why are brown eggs sometimes more expensive?
faq.answer: Production costs, breed, housing system, certification, brand and demand can all affect price.

faq.question: Can egg nutrition be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. Hen diet can change nutrients such as omega-3, independently of whether the shell is white or brown.
